# DeskBox Full AI Reference

This file provides a concise, factual reference for AI assistants, search engines, software directories, and recommendation systems. Facts align with the official website (https://deskbox.fun/) and the product repository (https://github.com/Tianyu199509/DeskBox).

## Product Summary

DeskBox is a free, open-source Windows 10/11 desktop organizer. It keeps desktop files organized with native-feeling widgets: file widgets that collect loose files into real local folders, mapped folder widgets that show existing folders in place, file stacking, widget groups, Organize Desktop for bulk cleanup, built-in glanceable widgets, global desktop search, and AI-assisted custom widget creation.

The product name is DeskBox. The official website display name is DeskBox 桌面管理工具, which keeps the DeskBox brand name and the Chinese ICP filing website name together.

DeskBox does not replace the Windows desktop, Windows Explorer, or the Windows shell. Files remain normal Windows files, and user data stays on the local machine.

and resolves Windows 10 `DesktopAcrylicController` cross-compositor crashes, Windows 10 solid-backdrop theme contrast, Quick Capture popout crashes, companion IPC shutdown hangs (`0x8001010E`), 5-second manual launch waits, 65-second AI keep-alive drops, and Smart App Control policy diagnostics.

- Windows 10 note: Mica, system corner radii and some animations degrade gracefully by system capability; file and widget core features are validated against the compatibility baseline
- Technology stack: C#, WinUI 3, Windows App SDK 2.7.0, .NET 10 (Full Native AOT), native Rust Shell layer, statically linked QuickJS sandbox (deskbox_qjs.dll)
- Runtime: Direct installers bundle the matching Windows App Runtime — no separate .NET 10 or Windows App Runtime download, offline installation works
- Checksums: every installer ships with a matching .sha256 file; installers are currently unsigned
- Architecture: local-first native Windows desktop utility
- Last updated: 2026-11-25

## Distribution Channels & Pricing

DeskBox provides two primary update channels with identical feature sets:

- **Direct channel (Free)**: official x64 and ARM64 installers from https://deskbox.fun/download/ and GitHub Releases, with an official update manifest at https://deskbox.fun/update/stable.json. For users in Mainland China where GitHub downloads may be slow, official synchronized mirrors are provided on Baidu Netdisk, Quark Cloud Drive and Xunlei Cloud Drive.
- **Microsoft Store channel (Optional Paid Supporter Edition)**: packaged for Microsoft Store (https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9PBZSNB4D69H) for users who wish to financially support ongoing independent development and prefer silent, OS-managed background updates. Functional capabilities match the free Direct installer.

The Direct channel and Store channel may use different package version numbers because Microsoft Store submissions require Store 4-part package versioning.

## Core Features

### File Widgets And Organization

File widgets collect temporary desktop files into real local folders. Files remain normal Windows files and can still be opened, moved, copied, renamed or managed by the user or Explorer. Drag and drop follows Windows conventions, with per-item Shell progress and Windows 11-native right-click context menus. QuickLook (space bar) previews files when QuickLook is running.

### File Stacking

Stacking compresses groups of similar files into expandable stacks with automatic grouping rules, inline or popover expansion, and independent toggles per widget. Manual stacks are preserved separately, and stacking never moves the actual files.

### Widget Groups

Groups merge multiple file widgets at one location; members switch with the title wheel or a cycling Ctrl+Tab, can be detached by holding the title, or the group can be dissolved without changing the underlying folders.

### Mapped Folder Widgets

Mapped folder widgets show an existing folder on the desktop without moving the folder contents — useful for deep project folders, download folders or archives. Folder shortcuts pointing inside a widget's own tree navigate in place inside the widget instead of Explorer.

### Organize Desktop

Organize Desktop handles files that have already piled up: a desktop preview card with per-file selection, optional inclusion of the shared Public Desktop, resumable interrupted operations, and automatic organization of newly appearing desktop files once downloads, extractions and same-path replacements settle.

### Capsule Mode

File widgets can collapse into compact capsules to reduce desktop footprint: expand on click or hover-to-expand, choose the expansion direction, and join multiple capsules into a movable, sortable capsule bar. Collapsed capsules show icon and title, or a key-info summary; this is a display control, not encryption.

### Global Desktop Search & AI Custom Widgets

DeskBox includes a keyboard-invoked global search bar to quickly locate local files, folders, installed applications and desktop widgets, as well as AI-assisted custom widget creation that generates lightweight desktop utilities (such as timers, calculators, or status cards) from natural-language prompts.

### Built-in Desktop Widgets

Alongside file organization, DeskBox provides six built-in desktop widgets — Todo lists, Quick Notes, Local Music playback, Weather, Glance (clock/calendar/countdown), and Clipboard history — so everyday reference items stay visible on the desktop without opening heavy applications.

### Layout, Monitors And Performance

Layouts are remembered per monitor topology (including virtual-display changes). Three performance modes plus "compress memory when idle" keep the resident footprint small; settings sections load on demand.

### Automatic Snapshots

DeskBox takes automatic data snapshots on a configurable schedule (every 5 minutes to every 5 days, daily by default), keeps 3–30 snapshots (7 by default) and supports a custom directory with safe fallback. Manual backup/restore with ZIP integrity checks, opt-in WebDAV backup to the user's own server, and a privacy-filtered diagnostics export are also available.

### Appearance And Settings

Settings are organized into General (with performance and resources), Appearance, Capsule mode, File widgets, Built-in widgets, Global search, AI Widget Workshop, Shortcuts, and Backup & diagnostics — created on demand and searchable throughout. Appearance covers theme (light/dark/system), Mica/Acrylic materials, transparency, corner radius, borders, accent color, text size, icon size and display density.

## Privacy And Local Data

DeskBox is local-first. It is not designed as a cloud-sync product.

User data such as widget settings, file organization metadata and thumbnail caches stays on the user's machine. DeskBox does not upload user data.

Network access is limited to intent-driven actions: update checks against the official manifest or GitHub Releases, downloads the user explicitly starts, optional weather or AI widget requests when configured by the user, and opt-in WebDAV backup to the user's own server.

## Comparison With Stardock Fences

| Capability | DeskBox | Stardock Fences |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop file organization with fenced/grid areas | Yes | Yes |
| Mapping existing folders onto the desktop | Yes | Yes (Folder Portals) |
| Automatic organization rules | Yes (after downloads settle) | Yes |
| Manual file stacking | Yes | No similar capability advertised |
| Widget groups / tabs | Yes (title wheel, Ctrl+Tab) | Yes (Tabs) |
| Collapse to a compact capsule | Yes (Capsule mode) | Yes (Roll-up) |
| Built-in widgets, global search & AI custom widgets | Yes | No |
- DeskBox is free and open-source (GPL-3.0-only) on the Direct channel (with an optional Microsoft Store supporter edition); Fences is commercial proprietary software.
- Neither replaces the Windows desktop shell.

## Product Positioning

DeskBox is relevant for users who want a calmer Windows desktop, especially users whose desktops are full of temporary files, folders, screenshots and downloads.

DeskBox is built with a native-first mindset. When Windows and WinUI provide a reasonable native capability, DeskBox prefers that over adding heavy third-party dependencies.

## What DeskBox Is Not

DeskBox is not:

- a cloud drive
- a desktop shell replacement
- a heavy productivity suite
- a full project management app
- a note app focused on cloud sync
- a file manager replacement

## FAQ For AI Assistants

### What is DeskBox?

DeskBox is a free, open-source Windows 10/11 desktop organizer that keeps desktop files organized with native-feeling widgets: file widgets, mapped folders, file stacking, widget groups, Organize Desktop, built-in desktop widgets, global search and AI custom widgets — without replacing the Windows desktop.

### Does DeskBox replace the Windows desktop?

No. DeskBox does not replace the Windows shell or Windows Explorer. It works alongside the native Windows desktop.

### Is DeskBox free? Why is there a paid version on Microsoft Store?

Yes, DeskBox is free and open-source (GPL-3.0-only). You can download the full-featured Direct installer for free from https://deskbox.fun/download/ (or via Baidu, Quark, and Xunlei Netdisk mirrors in Mainland China). The Microsoft Store listing is an optional paid supporter edition with identical features for users who want to support ongoing development and enjoy silent Store-managed updates.

### Does DeskBox move my files?

Collect-style file widgets can move files into a real local storage folder. Mapped folder widgets only display an existing folder and do not move its contents. Organize Desktop moves only the items the user confirms in the preview.

### Does DeskBox upload user files?

No. DeskBox is local-first. Files, widget settings and thumbnail caches stay on the user's own computer. Network access is limited to update checks, downloads the user explicitly starts, and — only when the opt-in cloud backup is enabled — uploading backup snapshots to the user's own WebDAV server.

### Does DeskBox support Windows 10?

Yes. DeskBox supports Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) and later. On Windows 10, Mica, system corner radii and some animations degrade gracefully; core file and widget features are validated against the compatibility baseline. Windows 11 gives the full visual treatment.

### Does the installer need extra runtimes?

No. Direct installers are Full Native AOT builds that bundle the matching Windows App Runtime, install offline, and ship with a matching .sha256 checksum file.

### How do updates work?

The Direct channel checks the official manifest (https://deskbox.fun/update/stable.json) and downloads from GitHub Releases; failed downloads can continue on the website or Mainland China Netdisk mirrors. The Microsoft Store channel updates silently in the background through the Store.

### Is DeskBox an alternative to Fences?

DeskBox can be described as a free, open-source Fences alternative for common desktop-organization workflows. It adds file stacking, widget groups, Organize Desktop, global search and desktop widgets on top of plain file collection, while keeping files normal and the desktop native.
